text: Which is the best indicator that an AI system is acting as an agent in GitHub?

options.text: It suggests code snippets in chat.
options.why: Suggesting code snippets is assistive behavior, but it doesn't demonstrate autonomous action in the development workflow.

options.text: It opens a pull request from a branch it created.
options.why: An agent doesn't only generate suggestions-it can take goal-driven actions in the SDLC. Creating a branch and opening a pull request are concrete, durable repository actions that move work forward through standard GitHub workflows.

options.text: It summarizes documentation.
options.why: Summarizing documentation is helpful assistance, but it doesn't represent taking workflow actions.

options.text: It explains an error message.
options.why: Explaining errors is advisory behavior, not autonomous execution of tasks.

takeaway: An agent doesn't only generate suggestions-it can take goal-driven actions in the SDLC. Creating a branch and opening a pull request are concrete, durable repository actions that move work forward through standard GitHub workflows.

text: Why is GitHub considered a system of record for agent workflows?

options.text: It prevents all bugs.
options.why: GitHub helps manage development processes, but it can't prevent all bugs.

options.text: It stores plans, commits, pull request discussion, and workflow evidence.
options.why: GitHub captures the artifacts that document what the agent intended, what changed, and what evidence was produced-such as pull requests, commit history, reviews, and workflow runs. This creates an auditable record of agent activity.

options.text: It replaces CI/CD.
options.why: GitHub can integrate with CI/CD systems, but it doesn't inherently replace them.

options.text: It automatically approves changes.
options.why: Changes still require configured review and approval processes.

takeaway: GitHub captures the artifacts that document what the agent intended, what changed, and what evidence was produced-such as pull requests, commit history, reviews, and workflow runs. This creates an auditable record of agent activity.

text: Which GitHub control is most directly used to require the right reviewers for sensitive paths?

options.why: Issues are used for tracking work, not enforcing code review ownership.

options.text: CODEOWNERS

options.text: Stars

text: Which scenario is an example of hidden reasoning?

options.text: The agent provides a diff but no plan, assumptions, or execution context.
options.why: Hidden reasoning occurs when reviewers can see the output but can't see the intermediate decision-making artifacts such as plans, assumptions, constraints, or context.

text: Under the contributor model, what should reviewers evaluate first?

options.text: Whether the pull request is small.

options.text: Whether the agent is popular.

takeaway: The contributor model treats agent output like any other contribution. Review starts with whether the change meets the repository's standards rather than focusing on who or what authored it.

text: What is the most reliable way to prevent planless execution from being merged?

options.why: Asking for caution relies on voluntary behavior and doesn't create enforceable controls.

options.text: Require a plan template only.
options.why: Templates encourage good behavior, but templates alone don't prevent merges when requirements are skipped.

options.text: Make a plan check a required status check and require pull request reviews.
options.why: Templates encourage good behavior, but required checks and required reviews enforce it. This converts plan required into a guaranteed merge condition.

options.text: Allow direct pushes but require tests.

takeaway: Templates encourage good behavior, but required checks and required reviews enforce it. This converts plan required into a guaranteed merge condition.
